newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Philippine president Fidel Ramos declared an unprecedented 60-day unilateral ceasefire, the longest truce, from December 1 to January 29, 1997, in the fight against communist rebels and Moslem separatists to allow people to celebrate the Christmas holiday in relative peace. (MANILA TIMES/PHILIPPINE STAR/CHRONICLE)

- Philippine vice-president Joseph Estrada and Senator Edgardo Angara, chairman of the Laban party, said they finally believed President Ramos will definitely turn over the presidency to a successor in 1998 and will not amend the Constitution to extend his term. (MALAYA)

- The House of Representatives committee on constitutional amendments has scheduled on December 3 discussions on a proposal to lift limits on the terms of all elected officials, including President Ramos (INQUIRER/TODAY)
- The Monetary Board, the policy-making body of the Central Bank, approved a two-percentage point reduction in the reserve requirement of banks to 13 percent from 15 percent. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Monetary Board also approved an increase in the minimum required capital of universal banks, commercial banks, and Metro Manila-based thrift banks in a move to bolster the local banks' financial capability amid growing competitiion. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- AsianBank and PDCP Bank have agreed to merge with the resulting bank having a combined capital of 6.6 billion pesos and branches totalling 140. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
